items.title: F1: caos Gp Bahrain, prima la pioggia poi problemi tecnici, il via con la safety car LIVE
items.summary: Hamilton costretto a fermarsi, nuovo rinvio per la partenza dopo quello di questa mattina alle 9
items.content:
Alcune monoposto, tra cui quella di Max Verstappen e Lewis Hamilton, hanno avuto dei problemi tecnici nel giro di formazione del Gp del Bahrain, dietro alla safety car, e nel caos che ne è seguito la direzione gara ha deciso di richiamare tutti sulla pit lane. In particolare, la Ferrari di Hamilton si è del tutto fermata in pista e gli altri piloti l'hanno superata prima che il britannico potesse ripartire. I problemi riscontrati sarebbero legati ai software delle monoposto, messi in crisi dalla bassissima velocità nel giro di formazione, che in alcuni casi sono stati resettati. La Fia ha reso noto che per la partenza della gara verrà utilizzato l'ordine originale della griglia, con Verstappen in pole position e al suo fianco Hamilton.

In precedenza la partenza del Gp era stata rinviata per la pioggia battente sul circuito malese di Sepang. Alle 9 in pista stava girando la Medical Car per valutare le condizioni del tracciato, che mostrava in vari punti ampie zone allagate tanto da rendere complicata la tenuta di strada della vettura. La pioggia non aveva impedito ai piloti di raggiungere la testa dello schieramento per l'inno nazionale, tutti riparati sotto ampi ombrelli. La pioggia ha smesso di cadere con forza sul circuito malese di Sepang, sede del Gp del Bahrain, e gli organizzatori hanno annunciato che il giro di formazione comincerà alle 9.40 italiane, 40 minuti dopo la partenza prevista. A seconda delle condizioni della pista, si deciderà se fare eventualmente iniziare la gara dietro alla safety car.

items.title: San Francesco, il presidente Mattarella ad Assisi per le celebrazioni
items.summary: Il 4 ottobre torna a essere festa nazionale
items.content:
Il presidente della Repubblica Sergio Mattarella è arrivato ad Assisi per partecipare alle celebrazioni per San Francesco patrono d'Italia. Che torna a essere festa nazionale. Ad accogliere Mattarella il sottosegretario Alfredo Mantovano, la presidente della Regione Umbria Stefania Proietti, con la Giunta, il sindaco di Assisi Valter Stoppini e il custode del Sacro Convento di Assisi fra Marco Moroni.

Fa in questi momenti il suo ingresso nella basilica di San Francesco il presidente della Cei , il card. Matteo Zuppi, che presiede la messa nella festa di San Francesco.

"In questa stagione siamo tentati e sedotti dalla cultura della potenza, volgare e invadente, ingannevole, frutto di enfasi mal riposte e di sfacciati ed enormi interessi economici, di nazionalismi che rovinano le nazioni, di campagne che creano il nemico invece di cercare quello che unisce". Lo dice il card. Matteo Zuppi celebrando da Assisi nella festa di San Francesco: "Il suo e il nostro - aggiunge - è un mondo segnato da guerre, terribili" ma "Francesco ci ricorda che la guerra non è un destino". "Non c'è tempo da perdere, il divisore imbroglia e fa credere che troviamo la pace con le armi e non con il dialogo e il diritto".

Il sindaco di Assisi Valter Stoppini ha acceso la lampada votiva che illumina la tomba di San Francesco, Ad Assisi. Lo ha fatto a nome di tutte le regioni, province e comuni italiani nel corso della messa celebrata nella Basilica superiore dal presidente dei vescovi italiani Matteo Zuppi, alla presenza del presidente della Repubblica Sergio Mattarella, del sottosegretario alla presidenza del Consiglio Alfredo Mantovano e della presidente della Regione Umbria Stefania Proietti. "Esprimiamo l'amore che tutti gli italiani hanno per te e imploriamo la tua costante protezione" ha detto Stoppini rivolto a San Francesco. "Vigila, Francesco fratello santo, sul nostro popolo - ha aggiunto -, illumina i governanti, veglia sulle sorti dell'Italia. Rafforza i vincoli di unità, solidarietà, fraternità. Benedici tutti i lavoratori e dona loro e alle famiglie prosperità e pace".

items.title: Come trasformare un MacBook inutilizzato in un NAS domestico
items.summary: Lunità può essere utilizzata per archiviazione e backup.
items.content:
Anche un MacBook con qualche anno alle spalle può trovare una seconda vita all'interno della rete domestica, trasformandosi in un piccolo server per archiviare file, effettuare backup o riprodurre contenuti multimediali. L'operazione richiede pochi passaggi e può essere effettuata sfruttando macOS, con un investimento minimo o pari a zero.

MACOS È LA SOLUZIONE PIÙ SEMPLICE

Il primo passo da compiere per poter sfruttare il proprio MacBook come NAS (Network Attached Storage) o hub domestico è quello di formattare l'unità per riportarlo alle impostazioni di fabbrica. Il consiglio è chiaramente quello di utilizzare l'ultima versione del sistema operativo disponibile per il modello in proprio possesso.

Grazie alle funzioni integrate di macOS, non è indispensabile installare un sistema operativo alternativo. La strada più immediata consiste, infatti, nell'attivare l'opzione di condivisione file, raggiungibile nelle impostazioni di sistema. Qui è possibile scegliere quali cartelle rendere disponibili sulla rete e stabilire quali utenti possono accedervi, oltre a fornire l'indirizzo IP.

items.title: Teheran: da Usa proposte ma Hormuz resta chiuso se non soddisfatte nostre richieste
items.summary: Ghalibaf: 'L'Iran combatterà e negozierà. Finita l'epoca in cui si perdeva tempo con richieste unilaterali'
items.content:
Il capo negoziatore iraniano Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf ha dichiarato che l'Iran non è né "entusiasta" né "intimidito" dalle azioni degli Stati Uniti e che intende "sia combattere che negoziare". Lo riporta Al Jazeera. "Siamo presenti sul campo di battaglia militare con tutte le nostre forze e li affronteremo con nuove sorprese; al contempo, utilizziamo gli strumenti della diplomazia per affermare la nostra superiorità in ambito militare e far valere i diritti del popolo iraniano", ha aggiunto. Il mese scorso, l'Iran ha comunicato agli Stati Uniti, tramite mediatori del Qatar, una serie di condizioni formali per porre fine al conflitto. Tali condizioni includono la cessazione delle ostilità su tutti i fronti, lo sblocco dei fondi iraniani congelati, la fine del blocco navale ai porti iraniani, la cessazione delle interferenze statunitensi negli affari interni dell'Iran, lo stop alla cooperazione degli Usa con gli avversari dell'Iran e la fine di ogni attacco statunitense contro il territorio iraniano.

Ghalibaf , ha affermato che Washington ha avanzato "alcune proposte tramite un mediatore" dopo che Teheran aveva proposto una tabella di marcia di 7 giorni per la riapertura dello Stretto di Hormuz. Tuttavia, ha sottolineato, gli Usa devono sapere "che l'epoca in cui si perdeva tempo e si imponevano richieste unilaterali è finita", che la posizione dell'Iran rimane "chiara e definita" e che "lo Stretto di Hormuz non verrà riaperto finché non saranno soddisfatte le nostre sette condizioni basate sul Memorandum di Islamabad". Lo riporta Al Jazeera. "L'Iran non è un Paese che definisce la propria grande strategia e la sicurezza nazionale sulla base dei tweet o delle interviste quotidiane dei funzionari americani. Basiamo le nostre azioni sulla condotta effettiva del nemico, non sulla retorica mediatica o su false dicotomie", ha aggiunto, citato dall'agenzia Irna. "Così come prendiamo sul serio l'autodifesa, siamo altrettanto fermi e risoluti sia nel difendere noi stessi sia nel portare avanti la diplomazia": è quanto dichiarato oggi dal mi nistro degli Esteri iraniano, Abbas Araghchi , citato dall'agenzia Irna. "Se i nostri avversari dovessero scegliere ancora una volta la via dello scontro militare — ha proseguito — si troveranno ad affrontare una risposta molto più dura di quelle precedenti. Tuttavia, se intendono perseguire la via diplomatica, siamo pronti a raggiungere attraverso la diplomazia una soluzione equa e dignitosa per porre fine a questo conflitto". In merito al nuovo piano dell'Iran per risolvere le controversie ancora in corso con gli Stati Uniti, Araghchi ha sottolineato che, se gli Stati Uniti accetteranno il piano iraniano di sette giorni, lo Stretto di Hormuz verrà riaperto entro i sette giorni. items.title: Benzina dall'aria? Il sistema di questa startup ne produce 3,8 litri al giorno
items.summary: Una startup newyorkese ha presentato un dispositivo in grado di trasformare anidride carbonica e acqua in carburante sintetico per i motori tradizionali.
items.content:
L'aumento dei prezzi della benzina e del gasolio alla pompa continua a pesare sul bilancio di famiglie ed imprese, riaccendendo il dibattito sulla dipendenza dai combustibili fossili e sulla necessità di accelerare verso soluzioni energetiche innovative. In questo scenario di forti tensioni sui listini dei carburanti tradizionali, riscuote interesse la proposta tecnologica avanzata dalla startup newyorkese Aircela. L'azienda ha svelato un dispositivo compatto, dalle dimensioni simili a quelle di un frigorifero americano, capace di produrre benzina direttamente dall'aria, dall'acqua e dall'energia elettrica rinnovabile, offrendo un carburante sintetico immediatamente utilizzabile nelle auto già in circolazione.

Come funziona la tecnologia: dalla CO2 alla benzina

Il sistema sviluppato da Aircela unisce tre distinti processi chimici in una struttura modulare formata da tre elementi esagonali interconnessi. Nella prima fase del processo viene catturata l'anidride carbonica presente nell'aria atmosferica mediante una soluzione liquida a base di idrossido di potassio. Successivamente, un elettrolizzatore alimentato da elettricità rinnovabile scinde l'acqua per ottenere idrogeno, rilasciando ossigeno nell'ambiente. Infine, l'anidride carbonica e l'idrogeno vengono combinati per sintetizzare metanolo, poi convertito in benzina sintetica pronta all'uso tramite un processo noto come "methanol-to-gasoline". Il carburante ottenuto è privo di zolfo, etanolo e metalli pesanti, ed è compatibile con i serbatoi, le pompe ed i motori a combustione esistenti senza richiedere modifiche.

Produzione di 3,8 litri al giorno

Il dispositivo mostrato da Aircela è in grado di produrre circa un gallone di benzina al giorno, pari a poco meno di 3,8 litri. Contestualmente, ogni macchinario cattura quotidianamente circa dieci chilogrammi di anidride carbonica dall'atmosfera, un dato che dà un'idea del lavoro chimico necessario per ottenere quantità di carburante piuttosto modesta. Uno dei pionieri del settore, Klaus Lackner, ha in passato sottolineato quanto sia complesso scalare questo tipo di processi mantenendo efficienza e sostenibilità economica. Per ora, quindi, questa tecnologia resta lontana dai numeri di produzione industriale su larga scala.

Un modello distribuito e design ispirato alla natura

La vera svolta rispetto ai tradizionali progetti di e-fuel risiede nella scelta di abbandonare le grandi raffinerie centralizzate a favore di un modello di produzione distribuito sul territorio. Spiegando la visione strategica e le scelte di design, Liz White di Aircela ha dichiarato fedelmente:
Progettando macchine compatte e modulari, possiamo produrre carburante direttamente dove serve, riducendo i costi di trasporto, semplificando la logistica e consentendo la produzione anche in località remote o difficili da rifornire.
Illustrando i vantaggi del modello produttivo rispetto agli impianti industriali tradizionali, White ha aggiunto:
Producendo molte unità più piccole, siamo in grado di abbattere i costi molto più rapidamente di quanto permetterebbe uno stabilimento centralizzato tradizionale. Questo approccio ci consente di scalare la produzione, migliorare continuamente la tecnologia e portare sul mercato carburante privo di fossili in modo più rapido ed efficiente.
Infine, soffermandosi sulla forma geometrica dei moduli, la responsabile del design ha concluso:
I nostri moduli esagonali si ispirano agli esagoni presenti in tutta la natura, per i loro angoli di legame stabili, la resistenza e l'efficienza nello spazio. Questo garantisce una scalabilità agile per diverse applicazioni e la capacità di disporre a nido d'ape più unità.
L'obiettivo di Aircela portare sul mercato il proprio dispositivo e avviare le prime installazioni, offrendo così un'alternativa ai carburanti fossili.

items.title: Vasto incendio in un camping a Peschiera del Garda, diversi feriti
items.summary: L'allarme è scattato poco prima delle 6 di mattina e l'intervento. Il rogo, ora sotto controllo, è ancora in corso
items.content: Un vasto incendio è divampato, all'alba di oggi, nel campeggio Bella Italia di Peschiera del Garda in provincia di Verona. L'allarme è scattato poco prima delle 6 di mattina e l'intervento, per quanto l'incendio ora sia sotto controllo, è ancora in corso. La struttura era aperta, quindi con ospiti all'interno e, a quanto si apprende, le fiamme hanno interessato una ventina di casette mobili. I primi report parlano di un ferito in codice rosso, sette in codice giallo e 16 in codice verde. Impegnati nei soccorsi venti vigili del fuoco con cinque mezzi oltre a sei mezzi del Suem 118. Le difficoltà dell'intervento di soccorso sono state legate anche alla presenza di bombole di Gpl e di vetture. A un certo punto è stata pure avvertita un'esplosione. Le persone ferite sono state portate all'ospedale di Peschiera del Garda, ma sono state allertate anche le altre strutture del territorio. Non è ancora chiaro da che cosa sia scaturito l'incendio

items.title: Il cancelliere tedesco Merz arriva a Kiev per una visita a sorpresa
items.summary: 'L'Ucraina ha bisogno di tutto il nostro sostegno'
items.content: Il cancelliere tedesco Friedrich Merz è arrivato a Kiev, capitale dell'Ucraina, per una visita non annunciata; lo hanno riferito all'Afp fonti governative di Berlino. Merz - il cui Paese è tra i principali sostenitori dell'Ucraina nel conflitto con la Russia - è accompagnato nel viaggio dal ministro dell'Economia Katherina Reiche, hanno precisato le fonti. "Mi sono recato a Kiev oggi perché l'Ucraina ha bisogno di tutto il nostro sostegno nelle prossime settimane". Lo ha dichiarato Merz in un comunicato diffuso dopo il suo arrivo nella capitale ucraina dove il Cancelliere tedesco è arrivato per una visita non annunciata volta a dimostrare sostegno al Paese nel conflitto contro la Russia. "Se la Russia non verrà fermata, la sua macchina bellica finirà prima o poi per rivolgersi contro di noi". Secondo fonti governative, Merz - il cui Paese figura tra i principali sostenitori dell'Ucraina - è accompagnato nel viaggio dal ministro dell'Economia Katherina Reiche. "Oggi dirò al Presidente Volodymyr Zelensky: 'Potete continuare a contare sul nostro aiuto'", ha affermato Merz nella nota, sottolineando inoltre l'importanza della collaborazione tra aziende tedesche e ucraine. La visita del Cancelliere tedesco giunge appena un giorno dopo l'avvertimento della Russia a stranieri e diplomatici affinché lascino la capitale ucraina, preannunciando nuovi e "massicci" attacchi aerei sulla città. Il ministero degli Esteri russo ha dichiarato in un comunicato che "la responsabilità di eventuali conseguenze negative ricade interamente su coloro che ignorano questo avvertimento". Mosca aveva già lanciato un avvertimento simile a maggio, ma i leader dei Paesi sostenitori dell'Ucraina hanno sfidato tali moniti, continuando a recarsi in visita nel Paese. Kiev è stata bersaglio di pesanti attacchi aerei; le autorità ucraine hanno lanciato appelli per ottenere ulteriori munizioni per la difesa aerea, necessarie a contrastare le incursioni russe condotte con droni e missili. Negli ultimi giorni, la Russia ha colpito diversi ponti sul fiume Dnipro e infrastrutture energetiche; venerdì, il sindaco della città, Vitali Klitschko, ha descritto la situazione a Kiev come "molto drammatica". Merz annuncerà un pacchetto di misure che prevede lo stanziamento di un miliardo di euro in aiuti militari e 350 milioni di euro per interventi nel settore energetico. Lo scrive Reuters sul suo sito citando funzionari del governo tedesco. È inoltre previsto che durante la visita venga finalizzato un accordo per la produzione congiunta di diverse tipologie di droni. Il cancelliere tedesco è accompagnato anche da una delegazione economica che comprende dirigenti di Siemens Energy, Hensoldt, Diehl Defence, Quantum Systems e altre aziende. Si prevede inoltre che Merz solleciti il governo ucraino a compiere progressi sulle riforme richieste dai partner dell'UeE, compresa la lotta alla corruzione.

items.title: Diretta F1 Sepang, slitta ancora il via del Gp. Hamilton si ferma, poi riesce a ripartire
items.summary: Sul circuito della Malesia si corre il Gp del Bahrain
items.content:
Il circuito di Sepang ospita il Gp del Bahrain , prova numero 16 (su 23) del Mondiale.

Grande partenza di Antonelli, si porta al comando davanti a Russell. Malissimo le Ferrari, Hamilton scivola al 15° posto. Problema per Leclerc.

Hamilton e Leclerc con gomma rossa, la mescola più morbida. Gomma da bagnato per Antonelli

Comunicato l’orario di partenza del Gp, via alle 10.33 ora italiana.

La federazione internazionale sta verificando che tipo di problema hanno avuto le monoposto durante il doppio giro di formazione e se tutto è stato risolto in modo da non avere problemi al momento della partenza della gara.

In attesa di comunicazioni sull’orario di partenza della gara, a Sepang ha smesso di piovere. Si partirà con la griglia definita dalle qualifiche di ieri.

Le monoposto sono tornate in pit-lane dopo due giri di formazione dietro la safety car. Nel corso dei due passaggi, diverse vetture motorizzate Ferrari – ma anche la Red Bull di Verstappen - hanno avuto problemi legati ai software delle monoposto, messi in crisi dalla bassissima velocità nel giro di formazione. Hamilton si è fermato e ha dovuto effettuare un reset sulla sua SF-26, stessa procedura seguita da Haas e Cadillac.

RACE CONTROL: The starting procedure has been suspended The drivers return to the pits #F1 #BahrainGP https://t.co/U6kq7wMDJ9

Diversi piloti, tutti motorizzati Ferrari, hanno avuto un problema all’acceleratore. Sospesa la procedura di partenza, i piloti tornano ai box. Slitta ancora l’inizio del Gp.

Hamilton è riuscito a ripartire dopo aver effettuato un reset.

Hamilton procede lentamente, problema all’acceleratore per il pilota britannico della Ferrari.

Al via il giro di formazione, si va dietro la safety car. Subito un lungo per Hadjar che riesce a rientrare in pista.

Si faranno due giri di formazione dietro la safety car per capire le condioni del tracciato.

La direzione di gara ha comunicato che il giro di formazione partirà alle 9.40 ora italiana (le 15.40 a Sepang).

"L'intensità della pioggia è rimasta costante negli ultimi 10 minuti e non sono previsti miglioramenti per i prossimi 5-10 minuti", ha comunicato la Fia. In pista sta girando la Medical Car per valutare le condizioni del tracciato, che mostra in vari punti ampie zone allagate tanto da rendere complicata la tenuta di strada della vettura. La pioggia non ha impedito ai piloti di raggiungere la testa dello schieramento per l'inno nazionale, tutti riparati sotto ampi ombrelli, ma l'attesa prima di entrare nelle monoposto potrebbe non essere breve.

The starting grid for the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia #F1 #BahrainGP https://t.co/r4COJmQaaJ

Continua a piovere a dirotto in Malesia, al momento la direzione gara non ha dato indicazioni sull’orario di inizio della gara.

Il via del Gp del Bahrain era previsto alle 9 ora italiana. A Sepang, però, piove a dirotto e per questo motivo la partenza è stata posticipata.

items.title: Trump cambia AI in SI e la Slovenia si ritrova con un tesoro digitale
items.summary: Lordine di Trump sulla Super Intelligence scatena la corsa ai domini sloveni .si
items.content:
A volte basta cambiare due lettere per creare un piccolo terremoto su Internet, e se c'è qualcuno che in questo momento è in grado di dare vista a scossoni simili, quello è sicuramente Donald Trump. Come raccontatovi qualche giorno fa, ora negli Stati Uniti l'intelligenza artificiale, almeno nel linguaggio ufficiale del governo federale, dovrà ora essere chiamata "Super Intelligence", abbreviata in SI. E la decisione è stata del Presidente, prima di essere ufficializzata.

Lasciando da parte il fatto che con Super Intelligence si definiva un punto d'arrivo dell'AI, ovvero uno sviluppo tale da eguagliare (o superare) le capacità dell'uomo, la cosa curiosa è che quella sigla coincide perfettamente con il dominio nazionale della Slovenia: .si. Quello che non tututti sanno è che il risultato è stata una corsa alle registrazioni che ricorda da vicino quanto accaduto negli ultimi anni con .ai, il dominio dell'isola caraibica di Anguilla diventato improvvisamente preziosissimo grazie al boom dell'intelligenza artificiale.

Secondo Registry SI, l'organizzazione che gestisce i domini sloveni, a settembre le registrazioni sarebbero aumentate del 2.199%. Il 30 settembre, appena un giorno dopo la firma dell'ordine esecutivo di Donald Trump, sarebbero stati registrati circa 11.000 nuovi indirizzi, mentre nelle 24 ore successive il totale avrebbe sfiorato quota 13.000.

items.title: Price cap carburanti in oltre 10.000 distributori, Urso: «Un esempio in Europa»
items.summary: Oltre la metà della rete carburanti italiana aderisce al calmiere dei prezzi dei carburanti. Per il ministro Adolfo Urso il risultato dell'iniziativa è superiore alle aspettative.
items.content:
L'iniziativa del calmiere sui prezzi dei carburanti raggiunge un traguardo importante sulla rete distributiva italiana. Secondo le ultime rilevazioni del Ministero delle Imprese e del Made in Italy (Mimit) e dell'Osservatorio prezzi carburanti, aggiornate a sabato 3 ottobre, oltre 10.000 distributori hanno aderito al price cap, superando la soglia del 50% delle stazioni di servizio sul territorio nazionale.

I numeri dell'adesione

Nello specifico, il 51,7% degli impianti presenti in Italia applica un prezzo della benzina inferiore ai 2 euro al litro, mentre il 52,2% garantisce il gasolio a un costo inferiore a 2,20 euro al litro. In termini assoluti, su un totale di 20.141 impianti rilevati, sono 10.413 quelli che erogano la benzina sotto i 2 euro. Per quanto riguarda il diesel, su 20.147 stazioni monitorate, 10.519 erogano il carburante al di sotto del tetto dei 2,20 euro.Questo meccanismo di calmiere dei prezzi, avviato inizialmente da Eni in risposta al sollecito delle istituzioni e successivamente esteso grazie all'adesione delle principali compagnie petrolifere come IP-Esso, Q8, Tamoil e Costantin ha generato un impatto positivo sui listini medi. La diffusione del price cap sulla rete nazionale ha infatti contribuito a spingere verso il basso il prezzo sulla rete stradale, sceso a 2,052 euro al litro per la benzina e a 2,247 euro al litro per il gasolio.

Le dichiarazioni del ministro Adolfo Urso

A commentare con soddisfazione il raggiungimento dell'obiettivo è stato il ministro delle Imprese e del Made in Italy, Adolfo Urso, evidenziando la risposta del settore e la rapidità di adesione da parte degli operatori. Il ministro Adolfo Urso ha dichiarato:
Un riscontro di gran lunga superiore alle previsioni: in pochi giorni il price cap ha superato la metà della rete nazionale.
Proseguendo nella sua analisi sull'impatto dell'iniziativa, il ministro Urso ha aggiunto:
Un risultato significativo che conferma la validità di un modello di responsabilità sociale che può rappresentare un esempio anche in Europa.

items.title: Australia investigating Flydubai co-pilot's links to country
items.summary: State police and the country's security agency are looking into the co-pilot, who attempted to take control of a Flydubai plane travelling to Israel.
items.content:
Australian authorities are investigating the links between the country and a Flydubai co-pilot who attempted to take control of a plane travelling to Israel.

The co-pilot is alleged to have attacked the captain with a crash axe during a flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv before passengers managed to overpower him and successfully take control of the plane.

The Australian authorities have not identified the co-pilot, who has been named by multiple media outlets including Reuters, CNN and The New York Times as Hamam al-Hammami.

The prosecutor in the UAE has said it is investigating the incident and any possible motives.

In a statement to the BBC, the Australian Federal Police (AFP) confirmed its investigation into "the man's links to Australia".

The investigation involves state police and the country's security agency, it said, adding that an update would be "provided at the appropriate time".

Sources familiar with the case, who have spoken to Australian media, have said the co-pilot was issued a student visa in 2014, and studied in Australia between 2015 and 2017, until he left the country.

The Australian Broadcasting Corporation (ABC) said the co-pilot's student visa was cancelled in 2019 as he was no longer enrolled in a course, making him ineligible for it.

Counter-terrorism officials will look at whether the man was radicalised in Australia, the ABC reported.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has said he was an Omani national.

The flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv on 30 September was carrying more than 170 passengers to Israel.

Two and a half hours into its journey, the plane plunged 17,000ft (5,200m) when the Omani co-pilot attacked the pilot with a crash axe , the United Arab Emirates prosecutor general has said.

The pilot flying the plane, Capt Smit Machchhar, described how he was lying on the floor injured when he realised the plane was sinking and he had to act, explaining: "I told myself to go for one last push to open the door from inside", which allowed the passengers in.

Two reserve pilots then landed the plane safely in Saudi Arabia.

Machchhar, an Indian national, was taken to a nearby hospital before being airlifted to Abu Dhabi, where he is reported to be in a stable condition.

The co-pilot was arrested after the emergency landing and is being questioned by Saudi authorities, according to Netanyahu.

The UAE's attorney general, Hamad Saif Al Shamsi, said on Saturday investigations were under way to establish the circumstances, motives and any links related to the incident.

He said investigations into the incident revealed that the co-pilot attempted to carry out a "terrorist act", according to the country's state news agency.

In the days since the attack more details have come to light about the co-pilot's employment history.

While working at another airline, Oman Air, US media reported that Al-Hammami was removed from flight training because of concerns over his radical views, and was given another role at Oman's national airline.

It is also known that, from 2020, he was studying on a distance-learning course run by Buckinghamshire New University in the UK.

He graduated with a degree in aviation management in 2023, the university said. It added he did not take any pilot training at the school.

items.title: MotoGp: Marc Marquez vince in Giappone, poi Martin e Bezzecchi
items.summary: Altra vittoria del pilota della Ducati davanti alle Aprilia
items.content: Marc Marquez ha vinto il Gran Premio del Giappone, 16/a prova del mondiale MotoGp. Sul circuito di Motegi, il pilota della Ducati ha preceduto le due Aprilia condotte da Jorge Martin e di Marco Bezzecchi, rispettivamente secondo e terzo. Quarto posto per Enea Bastianini, con la Ktm-Tech3. Grazie al successo odierno, Marquez si è portato a sole due lunghezze di distacco da Martin, che guida la classifica del mondiale. Alle spalle di Bastianini, hanno tagliato il traguardo le Aprilia Trackhouse di Raul Fernandez e Ai Ogura. Settimo posto per Pedro Acosta (Ktm), ottavo per Francesco Bagnaia, seguito da Fermin Aldeguer (Ducati Gresini) e Luca Marini (Honda), rispettivamente nono e decimo. "Era importante fare questi punti qui a Motegi e sono quindi davvero contento" ha detto Marc Marquez dopo la vittoria, che segue quella di ieri nella sprint e che lo ha portato a ridosso di Jorge Martin, secondo oggi come ieri, nella classifica piloti. "La gara è stata dura, stavo dietro a Jorge ma sapevo che passandolo sarei riuscito conquistare la vittoria - ha aggiunto il pilota spagnolo della Ducati -. Lui ha cercato di riprendermi ma ho alzato un po' il ritmo e ho chiuso la gara in tranquillità". "Oggi era davvero difficile battere Marc, mi devo congratulare con lui. Io avevo un bel pacchetto e spero possa funzionare anche per il resto della stagione. Sono comunque contento di essere sul podio in Giappone". Così Jorge Martin commenta il suo secondo posto nel Gp di Motegi. L'altro pilota Aprilia, Marco Bezzecchi, terzo sul podio, ha detto di aver avuto un "fine settimana duro": "Sono arrivato qui in Giappone dopo un grave lutto personale e ci tenevo a fare bene - ha spiegato il riminese -. Enea Bastianini mi ha messo in difficoltà nel finale di gara ma volevo molto questo podio e sono riuscito a conquistarlo".

items.title: UK Government Body Kept Files on People Criticizing Prevent Program
items.summary: Article URL: https://reclaimthenet.org/uk-prevent-unit-tracked-online-critics Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49951139 Points: 18 # Comments: 0
items.content:
The Home Office tried to keep the paperwork private until an appeal brought it into the light.

If you’re tired of censorship and surveillance, subscribe to Reclaim The Net .

If you are a British citizen and you criticize a government program online, that criticism can be collected and stored by a government-linked body.

At least that seems to be the upshot of the actions of the Prevent Standards and Compliance Unit (StaCU), “a body linked to the Home Office," that has been keeping “observations” of those who speak against the government’s Prevent counter-extremism program on the internet.

The “evidence” of this comes from documents the group Rights & Security International (RSI) obtained under freedom of information law.

The group has now revealed that in the year from March 2024 to February 2025, StaCU made 77 “observations” of people who were critical of the program online – and that most of these “observations” came from X, with some from Reddit. Mainstream media articles were also included, as were posts from or about several organizations, including Hope Not Hate, Maslaha, and the Open Rights Group.

The “observations” are filed as “open-source complaints” and stored internally by StaCU. RSI is unsure what happens to this data next, and who the government may be sharing it with. What is known is that the process involves “attempting to independently verify claims.”

As RSI’s Freedom of Expression and Belief Team Leader Jacob Smith put it, “You should be able to criticize government policy without getting put on a list.”

Smith also noted that the fact that the government “has been trawling X and Reddit to find out who has been critiquing Prevent” should serve as “a stark reminder that, in the government’s eyes, anything you share online is fair game and could go into a file forever.”

The Home Office tried to keep this secret and refused to hand over the documents at first, but RSI won an appeal to the Information Commissioner’s Office, and the documents were released.

As RSI noted, it is unclear if any automated tools were used to find the posts, and if not, how the unit “found” them, or what it does with the data it collects.

The case is not the first time Prevent has been in the news for its controversial nature and the way it is implemented , but it is a stark reminder that the British government has no problem treating criticism of its policies as potentially dangerous.

items.title: Zelensky ha detto che l’Ucraina intensificherà gli attacchi contro le raffinerie russe
items.content:
Il presidente ucraino Volodymyr Zelensky ha detto che l’Ucraina intensificherà gli attacchi contro le raffinerie russe di petrolio. Il piano è stato presentato come una risposta alla nuova strategia russa , che sta colpendo i servizi delle città ucraine per spingere gli abitanti ad andarsene prima dell’inverno.

Zelensky ha detto che l’intelligence ucraina ha ottenuto documenti da cui risulta che il presidente russo Vladimir Putin abbia approvato quella che definisce una «nuova dottrina». «Abbiamo visto dei documenti e sappiamo che li autorizzano ad attaccare le infrastrutture, la logistica e soprattutto le città, i paesi, ovunque: strade, scuole, ospedali», ha detto Zelensky. «Lo scopo dell’operazione è fare pressione sulle persone perché lascino la capitale e le altre città». I documenti non sono stati resi pubblici, e per ora questa è la versione del governo ucraino. Il governo russo non ha commentato.

Nel frattempo il ministero degli Esteri russo ha invitato i diplomatici stranieri a lasciare Kyiv e ha detto che la Russia continuerà a colpire la città in modo sistematico, descrivendo questi attacchi come una ritorsione per quelli ucraini sul territorio russo degli ultimi mesi. Gli attacchi russi di sabato hanno ucciso almeno sei persone in Ucraina e hanno danneggiato il ponte Nord di Kyiv , sul fiume Dnipro.

items.title: What to know about Brazil's election pitting Lula against Flávio Bolsonaro
items.summary: Polls suggest the election will be a closely run contest between the left-wing incumbent and his right-wing rival.
items.content:
Brazilians are voting on Sunday in a general election in which the two front-runners for the presidency bear very familiar names.

The incumbent, veteran left-wing leader Luíz Inácio Lula da Silva, will be challenged by 11 candidates, the most prominent of whom is right-winger Flávio Bolsonaro.

In the last election four years ago, Lula narrowly defeated Flávio Bolsonaro's father Jair, but the tumultuous aftermath of the election, which saw Jair Bolsonaro convicted of plotting a coup after thousands of his supporters stormed the Brazilian Congress, has had a lasting impact on the nation's political life and this election.

Jair Bolsonaro, the right-wing former army captain who governed Brazil from 2019 to 2023, will not be running for president in this election.

Not only is the 71-year-old barred from standing for office, he is also serving a 27-year sentence for plotting a coup after he lost the 2022 election to Lula.

Due to recurrent health problems, he is currently under house arrest rather than in a cell, but he has had restrictions imposed on him prohibiting him from posting on social media or making public statements.

Despite these restrictions, his shadow - and sometimes his moving and talking image - looms large over this election.

At the event where Flávio Bolsonaro officially launched his presidential campaign, an AI-generated avatar of Jair Bolsonaro endorsed his son's candidacy.

When pressed by the Supreme Court about the deepfake, Jair Bolsonaro's lawyers may have denied he had given his permission for its use, but there is nevertheless little doubt that Flávio Bolsonaro has the backing of his father.

While there are 12 candidates running for the presidency, there are only two who have reached double figures in the opinion polls, and they are Luíz Inácio Lula da Silva and Flávio Bolsonaro.

BBC Brasil's poll tracker shows them both hovering around the 40% mark, with Lula slightly ahead of Bolsonaro.

If none of the candidates gains 50% of valid votes in the first round on 4 October, the top two contenders will proceed to a run-off election on 25 October.

The opinion polls suggest a run-off is highly likely - but with a relatively high number of voters still undecided just days before the election, an outright win cannot be entirely ruled out.

BBC Brasil's poll aggregator suggests that at the end of September, 9% of voters were either still undecided, or planning to spoil their ballot, cast a blank ballot or not go to the polls at all.

Brazilians who are 16 years of age or older are entitled to vote and it is compulsory for those aged between 18 and 70 who are literate, with a fine imposed on those who do not cast a ballot.

Almost 160 million Brazilians are eligible to vote in this election and, with polls typically surveying just thousands of people, the end result can differ considerably from the indications given by surveys.

Lula, the 80-year-old candidate for the left-wing Workers' Party, has been president three times already.

He served two consecutive terms - from January 2003 to December 2010 - and was widely praised for lifting millions out of poverty during this time with the help of a cash-transfer programme called Bolsa Família.

The former metalworker left office with record approval ratings of over 80%, but his party was later rocked by huge corruption scandals.

Lula himself spent more than 18 months in prison between 2018 and 2019 after being convicted of corruption and money laundering, charges he has always denied.

Those convictions were annulled in 2021 , leaving Lula free to run for the presidency in the 2022 election, in which he beat Jair Bolsonaro by 1.8 percentage points.

When he started his third term in office, he vowed it would be his last, and yet his party endorsed him as their candidate again this year, even though he will turn 81 later this month.

There is no doubt he remains a towering figure in the left. But while his supporters described him ahead of the 2022 election as the "saviour of the Amazon", praising his commitment to protecting the rainforest, some environmentalists have been critical of some of his recent actions.

His support for exploratory oil drilling in offshore waters near the mouth of the Amazon in particular has drawn criticism.

Lula insists that he remains committed to eventually phasing out fossil fuels and argues that oil revenues are key to financing Brazil's transition to clean energy.

His government has also pointed to the reduction in deforestation in the Amazon - satellite data suggests the area deforested in the first half of 2026 was reduced to its lowest in the past decade - as proof that its policies were working.

During Lula's latest term in office, relations with his US counterpart Donald Trump have been rocky .

Referring to what Trump has dubbed the "Donroe doctrine" - his administration's national security strategy which asserts that US dominance in the Western hemisphere should not be interfered with - Lula has insisted that "Brazil does not fit into anyone's backyard".

In another thinly veiled reference to both his rival Flávio Bolsonaro and those in the Trump administration who would like to see the right-wing candidate win, the Brazilian leader has also warned that he would not tolerate "foreign and local enemies of democracy" interfering with the polls.

Flávio Bolsonaro, 45, is Jair Bolsonaro's eldest son and has been serving as a senator since 2019.

The younger Bolsonaro is running for the right-wing Liberal Party (PL) and, while he is widely seen as less confrontational than his father, he is appealing to the followers of the older Bolsonaro by promising to broadly continue in his footsteps.

During his time in the Senate, the trained lawyer has advocated a tough-on-crime stance, calling for longer sentences and laxer gun laws, arguing that "decent citizens" should be able to defend themselves from criminals.

He has successfully lobbied for the US to declare Brazil-based criminal gangs Comando Vermelho (CV) and Primeiro Comando da Capital (PCC) as Foreign Terrorist Organizations, a move that was opposed by Lula.

The younger Bolsonaro has also courted evangelicals and the agricultural industry as part of his campaign.

He has said that he will cut what he says are unnecessary regulations and "get the state off farmers' backs".

Quizzed in an interview with Globo in August on whether he still believed - as he had said in 2019 - that climate change did not exist, he acknowledged that there had been "extreme climate events", but insisted that these events were "cyclical".

Flávio Bolsonaro has actively courted Trump and members of his administration by portraying himself as a loyal ally during a meeting at the White House in May.

More recently, he promised to join the US-led anti-crime alliance that the Trump administration has dubbed "Shield of the Americas", should he be elected.

Up until a few months ago, Brazilians told pollsters that crime and security were their main concerns.

But in the weeks leading up to the election, a scandal involving a jailed banker accused of orchestrating one of Brazil's largest financial fraud cases has pushed corruption to the top of the list.

The banker, Daniel Vorcaro, is well connected and has ties to many powerful people in Brazil - both on the political right and left.

Flávio Bolsonaro acknowledged asking Vorcaro to bankroll a biopic about his father after voice recordings emerged in which he could be heard asking for 134 million reais ($25.9m; £19.5m).

Police have since then opened an investigation into Flávio Bolsonaro for suspected corruption and money laundering over the financing of the film.

But pollsters say Lula's campaign was also hurt by the Vorcaro scandal, after alleged links emerged between the disgraced banker and an ally of Lula, the Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes.

Moraes is the man who presided over Jair Bolsonaro's trial and has made a number of subsequent rulings about the conditions of his detention.

A police report suggested that Vorcaro had made numerous calls and sent a number of messages to a phone number which officers say is linked to Moraes.

The investigators say Vorcaro asked the person with whom he was communicating for help avoiding arrest.

Moraes has denied any wrongdoing but these latest revelations mean that, in the crucial weeks before the election, attention shifted away from the allegations against Flávio Bolsonaro to those against the Supreme Court justice.

Lula has tried to distance himself from Moraes, saying that "no one is above the law", but his rival has already pounced on the allegations against the judge to make political hay.

"Voting for Lula means voting for Moraes," Flávio Bolsonaro told his supporters at a rally, using the right's intense dislike of the judge to shore up his own support.

Brazil's president confirms two US government officials were denied visas over election interference fears

Trump says White House talks with Brazil's President Lula 'went very well'

items.title: Why don't more developers “use the platform”?
items.summary: Article URL: https://nolanlawson.com/2026/10/03/why-dont-more-developers-use-the-platform/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49950554 Points: 109 # Comments: 76
items.content:
For years, advocates for web standards, performance, and accessibility have implored web developers to “use the platform” . I’ve often been one of those advocates.

The argument is simple: why build something yourself, in JavaScript, when the browser can do it for you? Whatever you build, it’s likely to have poorer performance and worse usability than something the browser could just give you out-of-the-box.

I think it’s worth taking the other side, though, if for no other reason than to understand where the “platform-skeptic” developers are coming from. If “use the platform” is so obvious, then why do so many people seem to need convincing?

The most obvious reason is historical: for the longest time, browsers were playing catch-up with the ecosystem on top of them. Libraries like jQuery filled crucial gaps while browsers implemented equivalent APIs – and even then, you might have to wait for laggards like IE6 to age out before you could actually use them. Today, most browsers are evergreen (Safari is debatable, although ~7 times per year ain’t bad), but up until the 2020s or so, web developers had to deal with a decidedly lumpy web . In that environment, rolling your own is a sensible choice.

Another reason is familiarity: when you’re used to looking for React components on npm, that’s what you tend to reach for, regardless of the problem at hand. If you search for “sticky positioning” on npm, there’s no package that says “just use CSS position: sticky , you dolt.”

And often, even with a robust standard, libraries on npm would fill a useful gap between framework ergonomics and the platform underneath it. I always found it intriguing that many React developers preferred to stick to JSX and React idioms – raw DOM APIs felt “icky” – but were perfectly happy to use lower-level libraries where raw DOM manipulations are common. For example, a virtual list library might happily use raw DOM APIs for pure performance, while exposing higher-level primitives that a novice React developer could better grasp. In a sense, the ecosystem of React components led to a natural division of labor where those with more expertise packaged up unfamiliar platform APIs in a more familiar form factor.

Some of this effect was also driven by documentation. Many npm packages have lovingly detailed README s or websites with examples, tutorials, and screenshots. Whereas until MDN became cemented as the go-to place for web documentation (with web.dev as Google’s more future-facing arm), documentation for the web platform was scattered across blogs, StackOverflow , and sites like CSS Tricks . And many of these sites would just tell you to use a well-known library like jQuery or GreenSock!

If it were just about third-party libraries versus platform APIs, though, then I don’t think it could fully explain the antipathy toward “use the platform.” Developers who are lazy (or do I repeat myself?), and who just want a ready-made solution for whatever problem they’re facing, are unlikely to care whether that solution comes from npm, the browser, or copied off of someone’s random GitHub Gist. They want to solve their problem and move on. But there’s a different source of anti-“use the platform” that I want to explore.

For a certain type of developer, building things yourself is just more fun . And often the resulting code is easier to reason about, especially if you don’t have an encyclopedic knowledge of the web platform. And once you’ve built something, there can be a kind of IKEA effect where you want to maintain and tinker with your own homemade code.

As an example, let’s imagine you’re trying to build a modal dialog. You might visually understand how these are supposed to work: content appears on the screen, but the background is still visible although partially occluded, and maybe clicking outside the dialog dismisses it. So you might grab for position:absolute and z-index to position the dialog correctly – aha, but the background still scrolls, so you have to disable overflow on the body… And then if you understand something about accessibility, you realize you need to handle Esc to dismiss, and build a focus trap , and return focus to the element that launched the dialog, and…

For many developers, what I just described sounds like a nightmare (and a good way to build something that only half-works). But for many developers, this sounds like fun! Think of how much you learn as you start building this thing. And think about how you could start putting your own spin on it by adding animations, themes, an optional “close” button… Before you know it, you’ve built a library that’s ready to go on npm. That’s way more fun than just grabbing and calling it a day – what a downer!

And for many of us, before APIs like existed, this was how we learned the web platform ! Many of the people who now advocate for “use the platform” were once themselves authors of polyfills, shims, and libraries. I know because I’m one myself! I spent years working on tooling for IndexedDB , WebSQL , and other browser storage APIs as part of my work on PouchDB , which eventually led to me feeling confident enough to sit in W3C standards meetings and even open issues and pull requests on the IndexedDB spec itself. Without the forcing function of a gap in the platform that needed to be filled, I don’t know if I would have found the interest or motivation to get to that level of expertise.

Of course, doing it yourself is not always an unalloyed good. Sometimes it just comes from pure ignorance. On the web platform in particular, I think one of the reasons there was such a proliferation of JavaScript solutions to problems that could be better solved by CSS, for example, is that many developers just didn’t take the time to deeply understand how CSS works.

And to be fair, CSS has historically been hard to understand! There’s a reason the site is called “CSS Tricks.” Things like the clear fix , floats , and the min-width: 0 trick are hardly intuitive. Rather than trying to understand CSS’s internal algorithm, it’s often much easier to just imagine the imperative logic you want and then express it in JavaScript. Plus, for years CSS didn’t have a straightforward way to express common patterns like line clamping , textarea resizing , scrollbar hiding , etc. So of course developers built it themselves using the tools they already understood.

I don’t even think this phenomenon of “avoiding the platform” is limited to the web. It can apply to any developer working on top of a platform they don’t fully understand. For example, at my work, we use ClickHouse for storing various kinds of analytics data. At one point, my coworker and I disagreed about how to store large JSON data in a column: he built a system for compressing it before storage, whereas I put the data in a separate key-value store and only inserted the key into ClickHouse. It turned out we were both wrong! ClickHouse automatically compresses data , and as a columnar data store you actually get better compression across rows if you just let ClickHouse handle it. And the separate key-value store was just a poor man’s version of what a columnar SELECT already does.

I only realized these things after actually taking the time to thoroughly read the ClickHouse docs and then write a benchmark to prove my hypothesis. In the end I was shocked that we had built something that was slower and clunkier than what the platform itself could give us out-of-the-box. The parallels with JavaScript and the web platform were hard to ignore.

I’m sure that if you’re a developer on iOS or Android, or someone building on top of a game engine, or really any kind of developer building on top of any platform layer, you probably have similar stories. There’s a reason that the stereotype of the grizzled senior engineer is someone who can take a junior’s baroque tangled mess of code and replace it with a single line. The more you learn, the more you’re able to wield your knowledge of how the entire system works end-to-end to create the smallest possible contribution to it (and thus reduce your maintenance burden in the long run).

I’ve been trying really hard not to talk about AI this entire post (because I’ve done it to death over the past year), but of course I can’t help but wonder how AI coding will impact this phenomenon. I actually have both an optimistic and a pessimistic take:

In my own use of AI coding, I’ve seen both phenomena happen. I’d like to think that as models and coding harnesses get better we’ll start to veer more towards the optimistic outcome, but I can’t say for sure.

In any case, these are my longwinded and somewhat conflicting thoughts on “use the platform.” As a mantra I love it, because it succinctly captures a feeling I have when I’m looking at some overwrought pile of spaghetti code and thinking how much better and more elegant it would be if the author just understood the layers beneath them a bit better. At the same time, I’ve been that author, and I’ve felt the joy of building such beautiful, messy code (beautiful to me, anyway), so I think it’s worth understanding where such developers are coming from. For that reason, I’m sure we’ll be hearing “use the platform” for as long as there are platforms.

items.title: American money is flowing back to the Vatican. But at a price
items.summary: US donors hope Prevost will talk less about climate change and immigration and speak out more forcefully against abortion and homosexuality. But the Pope shows no sign of giving in to their demands
items.content:
VATICAN CITY – When the Vatican opened the safe after the death of Pope Benedict XV in 1922, they discovered it was empty. “So who is going to pay for the Conclave now?” they asked, with some concern.

They decided to turn to the young and wealthy American Church. A generous cheque promptly arrived from across the Atlantic, covering the entire cost of the papal election.

Now that a Chicago-born pontiff occupies the See of St Peter, the flow of American money to the Vatican has picked up again — but this time with a different purpose: to help the new Pope, or to influence him.

“There is a great deal of enthusiasm in the United States, and that enthusiasm translates into financial support for the Holy See,” says Father Anthony Ligato, assistant vice-rector of the American seminary in Rome. “And I think it will grow further as donors look to support the Church”.

Every April, the North American College holds its Rector’s Dinner, a gala fundraiser attended by benefactors. The most coveted perk is a seat at a table with a cardinal; seminarians serve as waiters. In 2019, about 350 guests attended. Numbers fell during the pandemic. This year, with Prevost as Pope, “we are at full capacity,” Father Ligato says: “450 guests”. The same generosity could also find its way into the Vatican’s coffers.

The Vatican has neither taxes nor a monetary policy. Its income comes from financial and property investments — a centuries-old portfolio bolstered by the sum paid by Mussolini in 1929 to settle the “Roman Question”, 1.75 billion lire — from ticket sales at the Vatican Museums, whose finances were badly hit by the prolonged absence of tourists during the pandemic, and from donations.

Every year, large and small offerings are sent to the Pope by Catholics around the world through Peter’s Pence — €54.5 million in total in 2025 — as well as contributions from the wealthier national Churches. The figures are not public, but Repubblica understands that the episcopates of Italy, Germany, Spain, South Korea and, of course, the United States are net contributors.

Alongside these two sources — ordinary Catholics and bishops — there are private funds. And with an American Pope, donations from major US benefactors in particular are once again on the rise.

To attract this flow of money, the Vatican’s investment committee, headed by the American Cardinal Kevin Farrell, has adopted a distinctly North American approach. The Patrons of the Arts are also looking to the United States and its donors, seeking patrons willing to finance the restoration of priceless works in the Vatican Museums. So too is the newly established Borgo Laudato si’ at Castel Gandolfo, which this summer hosted a concert featuring Andrea Bocelli, followed by a private meeting between the Pope and selected guests.

Before moving into the media world, Montse Alvarado, the young Mexican-born, naturalised American executive chosen by Prevost to head the Dicastery for Communication, worked in Catholic fundraising in the United States. As well as restructuring the papal media operation, she will undoubtedly be looking to attract new sources of funding.

More broadly, an entire constellation of foundations, associations and wealthy American benefactors now surrounds Leo’s Vatican.

There is the Papal Foundation , which this year announced that, thanks to the American Pope, “25 new families” had joined its donor base, as well as more than $15 million in funding for a “record number” of more than 144 projects in 75 countries. There is the Acton Institute; the foundation of the Napa Institute, founded by lawyer and philanthropist Tim Busch; the Knights of Columbus, one of the largest insurance organisations in the United States; and Leonard Leo, the man who selected Trump’s Supreme Court justices, and his Becket Fund for Religious Liberty.

These are wealthy organisations and individuals with a distinctly conservative outlook. Today, they are pinning their hopes on Leo having had little sympathy for Francis. They regarded the Argentine Pope as too critical of capitalism, too distant from American culture and too reform-minded on issues such as homosexuality. The relationship never really took off.

One episode has gone down in Vatican lore. Pope Francis decided to use a $25 million cheque given to him by the Papal Foundation to plug the financial hole at the Istituto Dermopatico dell’Immacolata (IDI), a dermatological hospital in Rome. The Americans took offence. Francis replied that it was his decision to make.

A row ensued and the following year the Argentine Pope cancelled his audience with the Papal Foundation. Major donors, explains Dawn Eden Goldstein, an American theologian and canon lawyer, need what is commonly known as the “golden handshake”: a photograph of themselves shaking hands with the Pope.

Years ago, she recalls, a wealthy member of the Legionaries of Christ, Frank J. Hanna III, managed to secure a photograph with Benedict XVI — who was decidedly no admirer of the Legionaries — by purchasing the oldest surviving copy of the four Gospels, the Mater Verbi Papyrus, and donating it to the Vatican Library.

Then came Pope Francis, who “put an end to private Masses for American donors”. Now Leo has reopened the doors of the Apostolic Palace.Leo, who as a good mathematician knows how to read a balance sheet analytically, has never shown much concern for the Vatican’s financial problems. The Holy See has a growing structural deficit, driven by staff costs, the upkeep of treasures such as St Peter’s Basilica, the worldwide network of apostolic nunciatures and the steadily deteriorating state of its pension fund.

But “I don’t lose sleep over it”, the Chicago-born Pope has said, perhaps also seeking to convey the message that the Vatican is not overly dependent on outside help.The actual impact of renewed American funding on the Vatican’s finances is not yet significant. In the past year, 26.1 per cent of Peter’s Pence came from the United States, amounting, according to sources, to “several million” euros.

As for private funding, Dawn Eden Goldstein is succinct: “Given how small the Vatican’s operating budget is, American donors could, if they wanted to, finance a considerable part of it”.

But at what price?“I think they hope the Pope will talk more about these so-called pelvic issues and less about the preferential option for the poor,” Goldstein says wryly. In other words: more denunciations of homosexuality and abortion, less on climate change and immigration.

“Or at least that, when the Pope talks about the preferential option for the poor, he won’t be too specific in identifying the kinds of practices or policies that harm poor people. Let me be clear,” Goldstein adds. “I don’t for a moment believe that Pope Leo will change the way he speaks”.

One thing is certain: the Trump administration is keeping a close eye on Leo. It can neither ignore him nor win him over with flattery.When the White House proposed that aid that had previously been cut off should instead be channelled through the Cuban Catholic Church, the Holy See readily agreed. Then, according to reports, came a request in return: appoint bishops acceptable to Washington.

Pecunia non olet — money has no smell. But principles are not for sale.

items.title: Nigel Farage: “We will never rejoin the EU: Burnham has made a very big political mistake and he’ll have to deal with Meloni…”
items.summary: The Eurosceptic leader of Britain’s right speaks to La Repubblica: “The Prime Minister has really put me back in the debate, giving me the biggest boost in my career. A second referendum would spell disaster for Burnham. I’ve kept quiet about Europe for ten years. Now you’ll see what happens.”
items.content:
DONCASTER — Nigel Farage is in good spirits after smoking a cigarette.

The leader of Reform UK, neck and neck with Labour at the top of the polls, arrives in an electric-blue suit at Doncaster Racecourse, in a city that voted overwhelmingly — 69% —to leave the European Union in 2016.

We are in Yorkshire, along the fabled Red Wall, home to white working-class voters and many former Labour supporters whom the king of the British right has won over in droves over the years.

After his decades-long crusade against Brussels and Labour Prime Minister Andy Burnham’s latest pro-European shift, marked by his bombshell remarks the other day (“the United Kingdom rejoining the EU is on the table”), the 62-year-old Farage is more determined than ever.

Speaking to La Repubblica and a few British newspapers, his message is clear: if London really wants to rejoin the EU, supporters of European integration will once again have to get past his barricades. That is why Farage has chosen Doncaster to launch his “100 Days to Save Britain” campaign. Burnham has also raised the possibility of a second referendum on Brexit, and the latest polls suggest that 60% of Britons would vote to rejoin the EU.

Isn’t Nigel Farage worried about losing the battle? “Oh, I think a Brexit referendum will unite the country wonderfully”, Farage defiantly answers, “I can't see anybody falling out at all. Families will all be at one with each other. Bizarre! How can you unite the country and then reopen this?

"And the second point I'd make is this: is Andy Burnham a pro-devolution prime minister? You would think, listening to him, that devolution solved all problems: pass power down, and life will be better and people will be richer. To even consider rejoining the single market, the customs union, let alone the European Union itself is the opposite of devolution — a massive transfer of huge powers up to an authority, whereby there's nothing Parliament could do to change any of it. So, I find the whole thing totally contradictory”.

But still, 60% of Britons would vote to rejoin the EU. “Of course they do”, Farage replies, “until you tell them it'll cost £25 billion a year. Until you tell them it'll mean joining Schengen. Until you tell them it'll mean actually having to recommit to joining the euro. Remember that the Leavers haven't made their arguments since 2016. The ‘Remoaners’ have made their arguments every single week. I mean, do you know what? I actually think that Burnham has made a very big political mistake here. I really do”.

Still, is Nigel Farage already in talks to create a new campaign to stay out of the EU, and are donors offering him any money to support that campaign? “It’s premature. I mean, it’s just 48 hours... The independence arguments have not been made for 10 years. We thought this is a given, but you know, I will from this moment on start talking about this again. I've barely talked about it for 10 years…”.

And what would Nigel Farage do if the UK actually rejoined the EU instead? “I'm not going to contemplate it”, is Farage’s stark response. “It's just not going to happen. Is Burnham going to sit down with the AfD, and Marine Le Pen, and even Giorgia Meloni — all people that, throughout his political career, he’s described as being the most appalling people on earth?

"This is not the same European Union we left. It’s a very different place, and all of this is predicated on Burnham winning the next general election. I personally believe that, while it may benefit him in places like Islington and elsewhere in London, in places like Doncaster it’s going to go down like a disaster.

And he's really put me back. I mean, he's actually put me back into the debate about the European Union. I've been quiet for 10 years. Now you’ll see what happens”.

Farage alleged that Burnham is trying to build some sort of coalition ahead of the next election, probably with the Lib-Dems. Why? “It's almost like he's sort of building a referendum campaign team before we even get going. He might calculate that it'll help them dig more deeply into the Green vote and the big cities. But here in Doncaster and across the ‘red wall’ in the north and Midlands, I think Burnham has given me the biggest boost in my career. I really genuinely believe so”.

items.title: Ridley Scott: “The Dolomites are the perfect backdrop for my dystopian world”
items.summary: Approaching his 89th birthday, the director returns to theaters with The Dog Stars, a post-apocalyptic drama shot almost entirely in Italy: “I wanted the landscape to feel completely authentic.” And now? “I’d love to do a musical”
items.content:
“I make movies for the audience, not for the critics.”These were the words of director Ridley Scott some time ago, speaking out after being snubbed for an Oscar yet again by the Academy. Now, following four nominations across an epic 50-year career—for Thelma & Louise, Gladiator, Black Hawk Down, and The Martian—he is finally set to receive an Honorary Oscar at the upcoming Governors Awards this November.

“It’s about freaking time!” Scott exclaims when we speak. “While I appreciate the recognition, for me, commercial success, cultural longevity, and ensuring hundreds of my crew members have a job matter far more than a trophy. But, obviously, I’m pleased.”

We meet the veteran filmmaker to discuss his latest project, The Dog Stars, adapted from Peter Heller’s novel and starring Jacob Elordi, Margaret Qualley, and Josh Brolin. In theaters since late August, the story takes place nine years after a super-flu pandemic has wiped out most of humanity.

Hig (Elordi) lives with his aging dog Jasper at a small rural airfield north of Denver, Colorado. He shares the space with Bangley (Brolin), a gun enthusiast who had been prepping for the apocalypse his entire life.

"It’s a story about loss, solitude, and the fragile beauty of a world on the brink of vanishing. An intimate, adventurous journey—a love letter to nature and life when all seems lost.”

How do you maintain narrative tension when the threat comes from desperate human survivors rather than monsters?

“Scaring people is actually very difficult. A world like the one in The Dog Stars genuinely terrifies me. When I talk about scaring people, I don't mean monsters lurking in the dark, jumping out from every corner. That’s a cheap trick. True fear is psychological—you have to approach it like a horror film, watching people slip on a banana peel. It’s brilliant when it creeps in organically, when you start sweating a bit and your heart rate spikes. That’s the key. It’s visceral, instinctual.”

Is there a message of hope amid the post-pandemic desolation?

"I hadn’t read the book, but the script was outstanding. To me, it was a dystopian narrative without the zombies; I had no interest in treading that repetitive ground. I saw this story as being about a world that has crossed the point of no return—much like the moment we find ourselves in today regarding global warming. We went through a perilous ordeal with COVID, alongside financial collapses and endless political bickering over who’s right and who’s wrong… It’s shocking how foolish human beings can be.

"If you stack two or three more catastrophic events on top of that, we lose control. Suddenly you're staring down the end of the world, with people running for cover to grab whatever they can. It can happen. I think the most dangerous thing right now is that no one is paying attention to people's desperation and hardship. Without wanting to sound pessimistic, I just hope it isn't too late.”

"Because they offered me a fantastic tax incentive—there are no big secrets there! The script was originally written with the mountains of Colorado or Canada in mind, but after thinking it over… the Dolomites were the better choice. The food is incredible and the people are warmer. I only had one firm requirement: the landscape had to feel entirely credible. In all my films, the setting is a character in its own right; it’s the stage upon which the actors interact. No story can survive without a meticulously constructed environment.”

"My job is always a gamble, but within that gamble, I have to be completely decisive. Otherwise, I’m wasting massive amounts of time and money. But if you don't take risks, you don't get rewards. I don't dwell on past triumphs or failures. The moment I finish one film, I launch straight into the next. I loathe the word ‘retirementì’—it sounds like a death sentence. I despise the thought of stopping, so I’ll keep going as long as my health holds up.”

One of the film’s central themes is that what is lost can be found, and enemies can become allies…

"Yes, and good things can emerge from terrible situations. If that weren't true, we’d be back in the age of the dinosaurs. I don't believe the planet will ever be entirely uninhabited; there will always be survivors. Right now, there are eight billion people on Earth, and we simply cannot sustain them all. Look at the tragic situation in Sudan, the thousands of unhoused people in Los Angeles, the severe food and financial insecurity everywhere.

"Wars, invasions, bombings—without wanting to sound overly dramatic, it reminds me of Germany in the aftermath of World War II, where nothing was left standing, as if an atomic bomb had dropped.”

If you could speak to a young Ridley, what advice would you give him? “Trust your instincts, without regrets. Just because you think something you’ve done is a load of bollocks doesn't mean it will be seen that way forever. Learn from the bollocks.”

“Stanley Kubrick above all, but also David Lean, Akira Kurosawa, Ingmar Bergman, John Ford, and Sam Peckinpah. Artists, every single one of them, each with their own ‘trick.’ Stanley was obsessed with the artistic vision; Bergman didn't give a damn about money; Sam Peckinpah loved violence—people think he invented slow motion, but he didn't. That was Kurosawa in Seven Samurai.”

And what is your trick? "A multi-camera setup. It allows me to shoot epic scale at an astonishing pace. I picked up that speed from directing commercials; advertising was my film school, and it taught me how to move fast. Making a movie is a tightrope walk, balancing art and commerce. Despite my age, I remain fiercely practical—I always come in under budget.” Is it true you first dreamed of directing as a young boy?

“Yes, it was my secret ambition. I thought it would sound too foolish to tell my parents, because coming from where I did, it was unthinkable. The film industry and the theater were like the dark side of the moon. I never truly believed it was a viable path.” When did your interest in art begin? “The only real talent I possessed from a very early age was drawing. I used to spend my time painting while other kids went out dancing. My parents thought I was deeply strange. But I got accepted into the Royal College of Art, which was unequivocally the finest art school in the world. That’s where I met David Hockney, a genius on par with Matisse. I couldn't compete with him, but I wasn't half bad myself.”

"I’m doodling as we speak. I draw on whatever is in front of me, constantly. When I’m not working, I paint all day. I get better at it every day. Shooting a film is just like painting— I treat the camera as my paintbrush”.

"Treasure Island. The Bee Gees biopic is on the back burner for now. Treasure Island has a brilliant script by Jack Thorne, who wrote Adolescence. I’m in a good place with it. I’ve cast Hugh Jackman as Long John Silver”.

You turn 89 on November 30. Is there anything left on your bucket list?

"I’d love to direct a musical in the style of Bob Fosse, whom I unfortunately never had the chance to meet. All That Jazz and Cabaret are the absolute pinnacle of the genre, largely because they are anchored in extraordinary historical contexts. But given that my mother lived to be 98, that’s a dream that is still well within reach."

You own an estate in Provence. What does that place mean to you?

"It’s my sanctuary. I’ve been going there for thirty years. I bought it as an old farmhouse and gradually turned it into a gem. Today it’s a family business—we produce wine, and we’re actually quite good at it.” Is winemaking similar to directing? ”Absolutely. Selecting the chemist and the winemaker is just like casting a film. I have a fantastic "wine director"—I’m lucky, he creates something truly special.”

items.title: Onu, 400 civili uccisi in Ucraina dall'inizio dell'anno, +55% rispetto al 2025
items.summary: Riscontrati livelli "scioccanti" di violenza sessuale su civili e prigionieri di guerra
items.content:
Nei primi otto mesi del 2026 in Ucraina si sono registrati in media oltre 400 civili uccisi o feriti ogni settimana, con un aumento del 55% rispetto allo stesso periodo del 2025. Lo ha dichiarato l'Alto Commissario delle Nazioni Unite per i Diritti Umani Volker Turk al Consiglio per i Diritti Umani a Ginevra, come riportato dal Kyiv Independent. L'ufficio di Turk ha documentato 15.280 civili uccisi o feriti nei primi otto mesi dell'anno, a seguito dell'intensificarsi degli attacchi russi contro le infrastrutture civili. Sul fronte, l'ufficio ha rilevato che quasi 2.500 civili sono stati uccisi o feriti dai bombardamenti aerei russi nello stesso periodo, il 62% in più rispetto all'anno precedente. "La guerra in Ucraina è una catastrofe per i diritti umani che cresce e si intensifica di settimana in settimana, causando sofferenze inimmaginabili ai civili e minacciando un disastro ancora maggiore in tutta la regione", ha affermato Türk .

Gli attacchi russi contro scuole , centri medici , condomini, ferrovie e negozi stanno provocando un numero crescente di vittime civili, mentre la popolazione ucraina vive in un "costante stato di paura ", ha affermato. L'ufficio delle Nazioni Unite ha riscontrato livelli "scioccanti" di violenza sessuale contro civili e prigionieri di guerra. Turk ha accusato la Federazione Russa di utilizzare tali "atti abominevoli per torturare , intimidire e costringere individui e comunità". Secondo il rapporto, dei 1.004 casi accertati di violenza sessuale legata al conflitto, commessi tra febbraio 2022 e luglio 2026 contro civili e prigionieri di guerra, l'89% è stato attribuito alle forze russe. L'11% del totale dei casi accertati è stato attribuito alle forze ucraine, con minacce di violenza sessuale che rappresentano quasi la metà di queste violazioni.

items.title: Debris found from plane that went missing off US coast
items.summary: The aircraft lost communication with flight controllers after significantly dropping in altitude, according to flight data.
items.content:
US authorities have found debris from a medical transport aircraft that went missing with six people on board.

The Federal Aviation Administration told the BBC it had lost contact with the Gulfstream G-100 plane just after 01:00 local time (05:00 GMT) on Saturday, while it was travelling from Bermuda to Boston, Massachusetts.

The search for survivors continues off the coast of Nantucket, a Massachusetts island, the US Coast Guard said.

Authorities have notified the next of kin of those on the flight, four Canadian nationals and two Bermudian nationals.

"Search crews located a debris field confirmed to be from the aircraft off the coast of Nantucket," the US Coast Guard said in an update on Saturday night. It added that ships, helicopters and planes were involved in searches that would through continue the night.

The plane departed from Bermuda's L.F. Wade International Airport at 23:40 local time, according to flight data from FlightAware, and was due to land at Boston's Logan International at 01:30 EDT (05:30 GMT).

According to the tail number released by the Coast Guard, the plane belonged to Latitude Air Ambulances, a company that provides international medical flights for patients returning home.

Among those on board were two pilots and two medical staff, both Canadian, Clarence Togeretz, director of flight operations at Latitude, told CBC News.

The crew flew to Bermuda to collect a patient and their relative, who are not Canadian, Togeretz said.

FlightAware's tracker shows the aircraft significantly dropped in altitude before its communications went dark, plummeting from around 7,300m (24,000ft) to 3,300m (11,000ft).

Radio transmissions shows trouble with communications between the air traffic controller and the pilot, the Boston Globe reported based on transmissions provided by LiveATC.net.

"You're coming in blind? Is that what you said?," the air traffic controller asked. "Are you declaring an emergency, or no?"

"You're coming in a little weak so I didn't hear what your response was, if you were declaring an emergency or not," the air traffic controller said, according to the Globe.

The air traffic controller later confirmed the pilot had declared an emergency.

An area fire dispatcher asked emergency crews just after 01:00 EDT to prepare to meet a plane with an "electrical issue".

The dispatcher later said "the aircraft has lost radio and radar".

The Coast Guard said it would provide an update on Sunday morning local time.
